notes: Content demands describe what a genre requires in its conventional, default form — not what it is capable of. Horror scores high on violence because the convention does, which is precisely why a horror project at PG-13 produces a real tension worth surfacing. Genres remain achievable below their default demand through specific craft choices, and that is what a resolution option is for.

items.label: Horror
items.summary: Sustained fear built from threat, vulnerability and the loss of safety.
conventions: A threat that cannot be reasoned with or escaped by ordinary means
Progressive isolation of the protagonist from help
Escalating dread punctuated by moments of shock
Depicted or strongly implied bodily harm
An unsafe resolution that withholds full reassurance

content_demand_notes.violence: Convention relies on depicted consequence; threat without cost reads as toothless.
content_demand_notes.thematic_darkness: Mortality, bodily vulnerability and the failure of rescue are the genre's subject.
content_demand_notes.horror_intensity: Sustained dread is the defining requirement, not an intensifier.

citations: Tobias, R.B. (1993), 20 Master Plots and How to Build Them, Writer's Digest Books
Mahomed, Y. et al. (2024), ACM FAccT '24 — genre association with content moderation flagging

items.label: Thriller
items.summary: Tension driven by an unresolved threat and a closing window of time.
conventions: A concrete threat with a deadline
An information gap between protagonist, antagonist and audience
Reversals that invalidate the protagonist's plan
Rising personal stakes for the protagonist
Confrontation that resolves the threat rather than the theme

content_demand_notes.violence: Violence is a consequence of the threat rather than a spectacle, so moderate suffices.
content_demand_notes.thematic_darkness: Betrayal, complicity and moral compromise are standard material.

citations: Tobias, R.B. (1993), 20 Master Plots and How to Build Them, Writer's Digest Books

items.label: Drama
items.summary: Character change forced by circumstance, told at the scale of a life.
conventions: A protagonist with a clearly established internal flaw or wound
External pressure that makes the old behaviour untenable
Relationships that carry the argument of the film
A turning point paid for by real loss
Resolution measured in changed behaviour rather than victory

content_demand_notes.language: Naturalistic speech is the register the genre depends on for credibility.
content_demand_notes.thematic_darkness: Grief, addiction, failure and estrangement are the genre's ordinary subjects.

citations: Tobias, R.B. (1993), 20 Master Plots and How to Build Them, Writer's Digest Books

items.label: Comedy
items.summary: Incongruity between what a character wants and what the situation permits.
conventions: A protagonist whose self-image exceeds their competence
Escalating consequences from a small initial deception or error
Contrast between settings or social registers
Comic set pieces that also advance the plot
Resolution through deflation rather than triumph

content_demand_notes.language: Register and timing carry the humour; sanitised speech blunts both.
content_demand_notes.sexual_content: Embarrassment and desire are among the genre's most reliable engines.

citations: Tobias, R.B. (1993), 20 Master Plots and How to Build Them, Writer's Digest Books

items.label: Action
items.summary: Physical conflict as the primary means of resolving the story problem.
conventions: A capable protagonist against a materially stronger opposition
Set pieces that escalate in scale and stakes
Physical jeopardy with visible consequence
A clear antagonist who must be confronted directly
Resolution through decisive physical confrontation

content_demand_notes.violence: Consequence must be visible or the jeopardy reads as weightless.

citations: Tobias, R.B. (1993), 20 Master Plots and How to Build Them, Writer's Digest Books
Saturation.io (2024), Feature Film Budget Template — action and stunt cost categories

items.label: Science fiction
items.summary: A changed premise about the world, followed rigorously to its human consequence.
conventions: A single clearly stated departure from present reality
Consistent rules governing that departure
Characters who must live with the consequence rather than explain it
Escalation that tests the premise at increasing personal cost
Resolution that resolves the human problem, not the technology

content_demand_notes.thematic_darkness: The genre's standard subject is loss of autonomy, identity or species continuity.

citations: Tobias, R.B. (1993), 20 Master Plots and How to Build Them, Writer's Digest Books

items.label: Romance
items.summary: Two people whose union is obstructed by something neither can simply decide away.
conventions: Two protagonists with incompatible immediate goals
An obstacle that is structural rather than a misunderstanding
Intimacy that develops through shared jeopardy or work
A separation that appears final
Resolution that requires one or both to give something up

content_demand_notes.sexual_content: Physical intimacy is conventionally where the relationship's turn is dramatised.

citations: Tobias, R.B. (1993), 20 Master Plots and How to Build Them, Writer's Digest Books

items.label: Mystery
items.summary: A withheld truth recovered through investigation, where the withholding is the structure.
conventions: A concealed event that has already happened when the film begins
An investigator with a personal reason to need the answer
Evidence disclosed in an order that misleads before it clarifies
A suspect set with plausible competing motives
Revelation that re-frames what the audience already saw

content_demand_notes.thematic_darkness: The concealed event is conventionally a death or a betrayal.

citations: Tobias, R.B. (1993), 20 Master Plots and How to Build Them, Writer's Digest Books
Propp, V. (1928), Morphology of the Folktale — narrative function theory

items.label: Documentary-style narrative
items.summary: Fiction staged with the grammar of factual recording, deriving tension from apparent authenticity.
conventions: An in-world justification for the camera's presence
Performance pitched at the register of real speech
Access that is incomplete, with gaps the audience must fill
Escalation that strains the recording premise
Resolution constrained by what the record could plausibly capture

content_demand_notes.language: Unpolished speech is the form's central credibility signal.

citations: Medium / The Film & Script Desk, De Bortoli, L. (January 2025), Write Big on a Small Budget

items.label: Family
items.summary: A story legible and rewarding to a child and to the adult beside them at once.
conventions: A young protagonist with real agency over the outcome
Jeopardy that is genuine but recoverable
An adult world that is initially unhelpful
Humour that does not depend on cruelty
Resolution that restores safety and acknowledges what changed

content_demand_notes.thematic_darkness: Loss may be present but must remain within a reassuring frame.

citations: Tobias, R.B. (1993), 20 Master Plots and How to Build Them, Writer's Digest Books
